findings.claim: The score formula (additive, floor 0.25, neutral 1) ranks a reviewer with one `no` below a reviewer that has never been rated, and its unbounded upper range collapses the weighted draw into near-deterministic top-pick selection.
findings.trigger: Ratings [no] → 0.25 versus no ratings → 1.0; ratings [30×yes] → 31 versus [10×yes,1×no] → 10.5.

evidence.observation: 'score = 1 + sum(yes) + 0.5*sum(partly) - sum(no), floor 0.25; a lineage with no ratings on this purpose scores its all-purpose score, else the neutral 1'.
1 + 0 − 1 = 0 → floored to 0.25 < 1 (neutral), so one negative rating is worse than no evidence at all; a 31:10:1 weight spread makes the top entry win ~73% of draws before exploration.
39 ratings across 63 consults and 15 distinct lineages — most (lineage, purpose) cells hold 0-2 ratings, so single-rating cells are the common case, not the exception.
Re-rating replaces the record and stamps a fresh `when`, so a 90-day window on the rating's own timestamp never expires a re-rated signal and can admit a consultation from years ago.

findings.verification: Compute the score for [no], [yes,no], [] and [30×yes] and check the ordering against the intent that proven reviewers outrank untried ones.
findings.remedy: Use a rate with a Beta prior — w = (yes + 0.5·partly + 2p)/(n + 4p), p = 0.5 — scaled into [0.25, 2], and cut the 90-day window on the ledger consultation's `when`, not the rating's.

findings.claim: The no-continuation-after-quota/auth/billing-failure rule relies on a narrow text scan and ignores the adapter's already-classified `$agyFailureClass` and `$agyFailureTexts`. Billing wording is excluded by the scan filter even though the classifier recognizes it, so a killed turn reporting such a failure can still get a continuation turn.
findings.trigger: An agy or muse stream reports a billing or quota failure that the adapter classifies but stderr does not contain one of the scan's keywords.

evidence.observation: the adapter records a failure class and texts before continuation.
the gate scans only eventError and selected stderr lines and never consults agyFailureClass/Texts.
the quota classifier recognizes billing/payment wording that the continuation filter omits.

findings.verification: Have fake agy return a quota or billing error only in its result event and assert no continuation process starts.
findings.remedy: Run every candidate failure through one classifier and include adapter class/texts, complete stderr, and event errors in the gate.

findings.claim: A quota, auth or transport failure occurring during the continuation is not represented in `provider_failure`: provider-failure evidence is built from the main turn's stderr/event error and the original timeout outcome, not the continuation's stderr or parsed outcome. Endpoint health can consequently show the reviewer available immediately after its continuation hit a limit.
findings.trigger: The main turn times out normally and the continuation fails with a 429 or unauthenticated response.

evidence.observation: continuation errors are kept only in timeout_continue.outcome.
New-ProviderFailure receives the main turn's evidence rather than the continuation's failure texts.
without that record, a continuation quota failure cannot mark the endpoint out correctly.

findings.verification: Make fake codex hang then return a 429 from the continuation; inspect provider_failure.class and the next availability check.
findings.remedy: Select the final failing turn's complete evidence for provider_failure and preserve its retry_after/classification.

findings.claim: Any non-empty Codex continuation output, or any adapter-OK engine output, sets `$continued` before substantive/schema validation and therefore suppresses the main turn's partial salvage. A continuation replying with one useless sentence can discard substantial salvaged work while `timeout_continue.outcome` still says `usable reply`.
findings.trigger: The main turn produces useful partial work and times out; the continuation returns non-empty prose such as `Done.` or invalid JSON, with format retry disabled or unsuccessful.

evidence.observation: Codex requires only a non-empty last message before declaring the continuation usable.
engine continuations are accepted on adapter Ok before local reply validation.
the outcome is fixed immediately and partialNeeded is false whenever continued is true.

findings.verification: Return a one-word continuation after a rich timed-out stream and assert that a partial file is still written and timeout_continue does not claim usability.
findings.remedy: Mark continuation success only after the same substantive and structured checks as a first reply; retain salvage until that point.

findings.claim: The salvage's `exact` manual resume command omits `-TimeoutSec`, `-ContinueSec`, `-Effort`/`-NativeEffort`, `-MaxWords`, `-SchemaTransport`, `-CodexConfig`, `-Artifact` and `-Range`, so it can resume with different endpoint configuration, limits and review scope from the killed run.
findings.trigger: A run using an explicit catalog override, custom effort or `-Range` times out and its printed resume command is executed.

evidence.observation: the command serializes only task, mode/thread, provider/model/engine, purpose, raw and prompt.

evidence.reference: the ledger records the omitted settings
evidence.observation: restarting without them does not reconstruct the original invocation.

findings.verification: Run with each omitted option, force a timeout, execute the printed command under fakes and compare resolved ledger settings.
findings.remedy: Serialize the complete replay-relevant invocation or write and reference a replay manifest.

findings.claim: The claim that an unknown-reset quota is out for exactly 60 minutes on every surface remains false for an explicit `-Provider` run: the `quota-unknown-reset` branch is conditional on `-RosterWalk`, so the same health record is `unavailable` in listings and panels but `available` with a warning on the direct run.
findings.trigger: A provider hits a 429 without Retry-After and is invoked explicitly with `-Provider` within 60 minutes.

evidence.observation: the unknown-reset refusal exists only beneath `$RosterWalk`.
the listing deliberately passes -RosterWalk and therefore takes the refusing branch.
a normal explicit-provider preflight does not pass -RosterWalk and retains the older warning-and-run behavior.

findings.verification: Call Get-PreflightVerdict with identical quota health, once with and once without -RosterWalk, and compare State after ten minutes.
findings.remedy: Make the 60-minute rule unconditional in the shared verdict and retain -RosterWalk only for fallback-message differences, if any.

findings.claim: `-Range` accepts a single revision as well as a revision range, and `git diff <revision>` then measures the mutable working tree rather than a fixed change. The recorded size can therefore differ from what the reviewer reads or what later runs measure.
findings.trigger: `-Range HEAD` is measured while the worktree is dirty or files change between measurement and launch.

evidence.observation: validation rejects option-like and spaced values but does not require a two-endpoint range.
the one measurement is used for the prompt, warning and ledger without binding it to a tree hash.

findings.verification: Run `-Range HEAD` before and after touching one tracked file and compare `range.lines`.
findings.remedy: Require `base..head`, or record and verify the worktree/tree hash measured; warn when a single revision measures the worktree.

findings.claim: The machine-readable providers rows (-Json without -Short) report `roster_position` as the FIRST roster position of a provider label only, so a JSON consumer cannot enumerate the entries of a multi-model label; the human-readable table's ROSTER column lists every position.
findings.trigger: A roster with two entries on one provider label (e.g. gemini pro + flash); read `codex-providers.ps1 -Json` and compare `roster_position` with the entry count.

evidence.observation: Line 314 collects ALL matching positions into $rosterPositions, but line 328 emits only the first ([int]$rosterPositions[0]); the engine-label loop repeats this at line 384, while the text table joins every position at line 440.

findings.verification: Point CODEX_CONSULT_ROSTER at a two-models-one-label roster, run `-Json`, and confirm `roster_position` covers only the first entry while `-Short -Json` entries cover both.
findings.remedy: Emit `roster_positions` (array) alongside `roster_position` (first, for compatibility), or document that per-entry enumeration lives only in `-Short -Json` entries.

findings.claim: Test-UsableOutcome accepts ANY bridge_outcome with the prefix 'usable reply (' as a usable reply, so any future outcome string with that shape silently inherits health-clearing, RecentUsable sign-in evidence, and scoreboard-usable counting.
findings.trigger: A future code path records an outcome such as 'usable reply (draft)' or 'usable reply (partial)'.

evidence.observation: The function returns true for exact 'usable reply' or any string starting with 'usable reply ('; today only line 3390 of codex-consult.ps1 produces such a string, and the predicate feeds Get-EndpointHealth (Ok records) and RecentUsable.

findings.verification: Grep producers of outcomes starting with 'usable reply (' and confirm the set is closed to line 3390, or add a unit case asserting 'usable reply (draft)' is not usable.
findings.remedy: Match the two known outcome strings exactly (or centralize an outcome enum) so new suffixed outcomes fail closed.
